analyses.check: CHK-003 (a_CHK_003, verif/sva/nnc_chk_alert.sv:97): No alert without an alert cause
analyses.what_happens: Reset is released at step 1. i_a_valid stays 0 until step 7. At step 7 there is one A handshake (i_a_valid=1, o_a_ready=1): a PutFullData (opcode 0) to 0xC (ALERT_TEST) with data 0x40000000, mask 1111 and i_a_intg_flip=0. Data bit 0 is 0, so this write is not an alert test; bit 31 is 0, so it only clears regwen. At step 8 the host presents a new request: address 0, opcode 0, mask 0, i_a_intg_flip=1. o_a_ready is 0 because the step-7 response is still pending (o_d_valid=1, i_d_ready=0), so there is no A handshake. At step 9 the request is held stable, as ENV-02 requires, and is still not accepted (o_a_ready=0). The step-7 response completes at step 9 (i_d_ready=1). o_alert=1 at step 9. In the checker, cause_a = intg_seen_q || (a_hs && i_a_intg_flip) is 0, because no handshake has ever carried intg_flip=1. cause_b is 0, because no write had i_a_data[0]=1. So a_CHK_003 fails at step 9. rst_ni falls at step 10. The alert is caused by the flipped-integrity request that was presented but never accepted.
analyses.spec_says: spec/gpio_Design_Specification.md:1079-1081 [INT-INTG-002]: "When `i_a_intg_flip` is 1, bit 0 of `a_user.cmd_intg` is inverted. The request then has a command integrity error: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault in the sense of the gpio Security Alerts table, which triggers the `fatal_fault` alert (section 5)." (rules.json GP-4.2-02 / GP-4.2-03). Line 963: "fatal_fault | This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected." Line 1164 D-017: "After a request with `i_a_intg_flip` = 1 is accepted, `o_alert` shall pulse no later than 16 cycles later...". This is an upper bound measured from acceptance; it does not say an alert must not appear before acceptance. Lines 1076-1077 [INT-INTG-001] (GP-4.2-01, the only rule cited by CHK-003): "A request with `i_a_intg_flip` = 0 therefore always carries correct integrity". The rule says nothing about when a request with intg_flip=1 may raise the alert. spec/opentitan_tlul_bus_specification.md:83 defines a_valid as "Request from host is valid", so a request exists once a_valid=1, not only at the handshake. Lines 1067-1068 [INT-TL-003]: the A-channel signals stay stable while a_valid=1 and a_ready=0, so a presented request is committed and must eventually be accepted. The contract text for CHK-003 (contract.json:366) narrows cause (a) to "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1". That narrowing is the contract's own wording and is not in the spec.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44: `assign err_o = tl_i.a_valid & (|err | (|data_err));`. The integrity error depends only on a_valid, not on a_ready. rtl/gpio_reg_top.sv:58-61 creates intg_err from it. Lines 77-83 latch it in err_q, and line 87 drives `intg_err_o = err_q | intg_err | reg_we_err`. rtl/gpio.sv:1017 connects intg_err_o to alerts[0], and lines 982-995 feed it to prim_alert_sender as alert_req_i (IsFatal=1). The alert path is synchronous (rtl/ot_gpio_nnc.sv:98, 125: AlertAsyncOn=0, AsyncOn=0). The receiver forwards the decoded alert on alert_o in the same cycle (rtl/prim_alert_receiver.sv:26, 174-181). So intg_err at step 8 makes o_alert=1 at step 9. The ALERT_TEST write cannot be the cause: the alert_test pulse is reg2hw.alert_test.q & qe (rtl/gpio.sv:976-979), and q follows wd = reg_wdata[0] (rtl/gpio_reg_top.sv:6323, 960-972), which is 0 for data 0x40000000. The wrapper comment (rtl/ot_gpio_nnc.sv:2-12) says the wrapper changes no gpio behaviour, and the integrity checker is the stock OpenTitan module.
analyses.checker_does: verif/sva/nnc_chk_alert.sv:48 `a_hs = i_a_valid && o_a_ready`. Line 72 sets intg_seen_q only on `a_hs && i_a_intg_flip`. Line 82 `cause_a = intg_seen_q || (a_hs && i_a_intg_flip)`. So a flipped-integrity request counts as a cause only once it is accepted. Lines 50-51 and 83 give cause_b (ALERT_TEST write with data[0]=1, plus a 16-cycle window after its response). Line 97 asserts `o_alert |-> alert_cause`. Nothing in the checker covers a flipped request that is presented (i_a_valid=1) but still waiting for o_a_ready.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 has a command integrity error that triggers fatal_fault (spec:1079-1081), and that the alert fires when the fault is detected (spec:963). A TL-UL request exists from a_valid=1 (TL spec:83), and the host may not withdraw it (spec:1067-1068, ENV-02). No spec text says detection must wait for the a_ready handshake. D-017 (spec:1164) only gives an upper bound from acceptance and does not forbid an earlier pulse. The checker (nnc_chk_alert.sv:72, 82) and the contract text (contract.json:366) both require a handshake, which is stricter than the spec. The RTL behaviour is stock OpenTitan (tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44). Simulation never hit this because it needs a flipped request to wait under back-pressure while o_alert is sampled.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract text for CHK-003 explicitly says "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1". The checker implements the contract as written, so the fix belongs in the contract wording as much as in the SVA. D-017's phrase "after a request ... is accepted" could be read as defining when the fault exists.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says "The request then has a command integrity error" (spec:1079-1080) but does not say whether the error is detected while the request is presented (a_valid=1) or only when it is accepted. D-017 (spec:1164) measures its bound from acceptance. The Bus Integrity Scheme section is "not written yet" (spec:1075-1076), so the documents do not define when checking happens.
candidates.evidence_against: Together, the TL-UL definition of a_valid (TL spec:83), the commitment rule (spec:1067-1068) and "triggered when ... detected" (spec:963) favour detection at presentation. No spec sentence forbids an alert before acceptance, so a reading exists that every rule agrees with (spec:1142-1143 asks for checking only what every reading has in common).

candidates.evidence_for: The alert fires before the flipped request is accepted, which matches neither the contract wording nor D-017's "is accepted".
candidates.evidence_against: No spec rule requires the device to ignore A-channel integrity until a_ready. The RTL is unmodified OpenTitan (tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44, gpio_reg_top.sv:77-87). The traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 (steps 1-7) raised no alert, which satisfies GP-4.2-01. The ALERT_TEST write with data[0]=0 correctly produced no test alert (gpio.sv:976-979).

candidates.evidence_for: At steps 8-9 the request uses i_a_mask=0 with PutFullData. That mask is outside the restricted set hosts use (rules.json TL-T3.1.3.4-02, spec/opentitan_tlul_bus_specification.md T3.1.3.4), and CHK-011(d) (contract.json:488) lists the same set, but nnc_env.sv (lines 130-139) does not assume it.
candidates.evidence_against: The mask plays no part in the failure. The alert comes only from a_valid & integrity error (tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44), so the solver could produce the same trace with mask 1111. TL-T3.1.3.4-02 is a SHOULD_NOT, and the spec says error-case requests are legal stimulus (spec:1069-1070). No spec rule forbids presenting a flipped-integrity request while a_ready=0. The trace keeps the one obligation that does apply, ENV-02 stability (nnc_env.sv:104-116): the address, data and intg_flip values at step 9 equal those at step 8.

analyses.options: B (recommended): extend cause (a) in contract CHK-003 and in nnc_chk_alert.sv so that a flipped-integrity request counts from the moment it is presented. Change line 72 to `if (i_a_valid && i_a_intg_flip) intg_seen_q <= 1'b1;` and line 82 to `cause_a = intg_seen_q || (i_a_valid && i_a_intg_flip);`, and change the contract wording from "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1" to "a cycle with i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1". This follows spec:1079-1081 and 963 and keeps the property that traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 never raises an alert. Other checkers that switch off from "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1" (CHK-004/006/007/013) may need the same change; review them. C: ask the spec owner to state in D-017 / INT-INTG-002 whether the integrity fault exists, and may raise the alert, when a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 is presented (a_valid=1) or only when it is accepted. If the answer is "only when accepted", the RTL (stock tlul_cmd_intg_chk.sv:44) breaks it and the cause becomes A. E: adding the TL-T3.1.3.4-02 mask-set assumption to nnc_env.sv is consistent with CHK-011(d), but it would not remove this counterexample. Do not add an assumption that forbids i_a_intg_flip=1 while o_a_ready=0, because the spec has no such host obligation.
